claims.wording: On the tested native platforms, the full correctness suite passed: Windows x64 58/58 and Linux ARM64 62/62.
The native abrupt-termination recovery campaign completed 100/100 successful runs on Windows and 100/100 on Linux.
H6 task accuracy was 1.0 in every promotion repetition on both tested platforms.

At 32 workers, H8 retained a median 4 WAL records per ingest while median physical WAL syncs per ingest were 0.763 on Windows and 0.314 on Linux, demonstrating measured group batching on both tested systems.
Within each tested host, median H8 throughput increased from 1 to 32 workers (Windows 264.00→749.48 ops/s; Linux 129.13→1143.26 ops/s).
Real SQLite and RocksDB adapters completed their matched durable single-key workloads with correctness PASS on both tested platforms.

FAISS IndexFlatL2 default execution passed correctness on the tested Linux ARM64 configuration, while the tested Windows configuration exhibited transient default-path retrieval failures; the separate Windows single-thread diagnostic passed.
SynapseFS or the SymbioRAP Memory Engine is faster than SQLite or RocksDB.
SynapseFS or the Memory Engine is faster than FAISS.
Absolute Windows-versus-Linux performance differences demonstrate operating-system or architecture superiority.
The benchmark establishes universal best-of-breed performance.
